subject: Question: token-level vs final-output persistence
messages:
From: Sarah Patel <sarah.patel@brightbank.com>
To: jonas_weber@redwood.ai
Cc: BrightBank Security <security@brightbank.com>
Date: Tue, 10 Jun 2025 09:15:00 -0700
Subject: Question: token-level vs final-output persistence

Hi Jonas,

Quick one from our security team as we go through procurement: can you confirm Redwood's default behaviour for the hosted API in terms of what is persisted by default? Specifically we need answers to:  

1) Are streamed (token-by-token) fragments buffered and stored after a session completes?  
2) Does the platform persist any intermediate model state (KV cache, attention cache) off GPU to long-term storage?  
3) Are final generation outputs retained by Redwood, and if so what is the default time window and the opt-out mechanism?  

I've attached a short questionnaire that lists the fields the auditors want filled out. Also we need clarity on what evidence you can provide for deletion (proof of erasure / audit logs). Can you put together a concise table we can include in the security pack?

Thanks — we need this for BrightBank's security signoff this week.

Cheers,
Sarah Patel
Security Operations
BrightBank

Attachment: brightbank-data-questionnaire.xlsx
From: jonas_weber@redwood.ai
To: Sarah Patel <sarah.patel@brightbank.com>
Cc: kimberly_park@redwood.ai, grace_oconnor@redwood.ai
Date: Tue, 10 Jun 2025 11:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Question: token-level vs final-output persistence

Sarah — thanks for the clear list. We'll get you a short, exportable table you can drop into the security pack. Initial answers (high level):

- Streamed token fragments: ephemeral by default. Streaming buffers exist transiently during the request lifecycle and are not persisted to object storage; they are not searchable or indexed.
- KV / attention cache: never persisted off-device outside GPU memory for hosted sessions. We do not write per-session KV caches to durable storage.
- Final outputs (completed responses): retained by default in hosted US for diagnostics and regression monitoring for 30 days unless the customer opts out. Opt-out is available via an API capture flag (x-redwood-capture: false) and via account-level settings for Dedicated/Private.

I'll attach a short draft summary and loop Kim for the erasure evidence details. If you want, we can do a 30-minute call this week to walk procurement through the table.

Cheers,
Jonas Weber
Senior Product Manager, Security & Compliance
Redwood Inference

Thanks Jonas — useful start. Two follow-ups:  

1) For investigations we sometimes need copies to be retained longer than the default window. Is there an SLA-backed exception process to retain for a specific case?  
2) If final outputs are retained for 30 days, what automated redaction / PII suppression tooling do you offer before storage? Do you provide options to pseudonymize or hash sensitive fields at capture time?

If you can answer those in the table that would be ideal.

-Sarah
From: kimberly_park@redwood.ai
To: Sarah Patel <sarah.patel@brightbank.com>
Cc: jonas_weber@redwood.ai, grace_oconnor@redwood.ai
Date: Wed, 11 Jun 2025 10:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Question: token-level vs final-output persistence

Hi Sarah — jumping in with the operational details so you have a single doc to share. Below is a compact FAQ and the default windows for hosted US; we can supply a short variant for EU residency on request.

Default capture windows (hosted API, US region) — current defaults:
- Request inputs (raw user query + metadata): retained 30 days by default for diagnostics and quality monitoring. Customers can set capture=false to avoid retention.
- Final model responses: retained 30 days by default. This retention supports regen debugging, evals, and anomaly investigation.
- Streamed fragments / token buffers: transient; not written to durable storage and expire immediately after session completion (effectively < 60 seconds).
- Model runtime artifacts (KV / attention caches): ephemeral in GPU memory only; not persisted to object storage.
- Embeddings & vectors: stored only when customer calls embeddings endpoints; retention follows embeddings configuration and can be zeroed on request.
- Aggregated telemetry & anonymized metrics: retained 90 days for operational monitoring; these are aggregated and do not contain full user content.

Opt-outs and controls:
- Per-request capture header: x-redwood-capture: false — preventing both request and final output from being written to the post-processing stores.
- Account-level capture policy: available for Dedicated/Private customers and via an account setting for hosted customers on contract.
- Data minimization hooks: we offer a pre-capture transform webhook customers can configure to strip or pseudonymize fields before storage. This can be turned on per-route.

Erasure / evidence process:
- Ad-hoc retention extension: we support SLA exceptions for legal/incident investigations through a formal ticket; retained artifacts for an exception are marked and stored in a limited-access bucket for the requested window.
- Proof of deletion: when data is purged we provide an audit entry (timestamped) and a deletion manifest describing object keys removed; for enterprise customers we can deliver a signed erasure certificate.
- Audit logs: immutable audit trail of access and retention exceptions is available as part of our Private offering; hosted customers can request export for audits.

Next steps:
1) I'll update the draft table with the above windows and the opt-out flags.
2) If BrightBank wants EU residency, tell us the preferred region (eu-west-1 / eu-central-1) and we will produce a region-specific capture table and export path.

Attachment: erase-evidence-playbook.pdf
